name: Dyaberdyaber
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Nekes, Hermann & Ernest A. Worms [1953] 2006 (ed. William McGregor). Australian Languages. Mouton. Covers Nyulnyulan varieties incl. Djaberdjaber; not accessible online.
earlier_scan.note: Nekes & Worms materials are the only substantial documentation; may contain accent notes for Dyaberdyaber.

sources.citation: McGregor, William. 2011. The Nyulnyul language of Dampier Land, Western Australia. Pacific Linguistics 632. p. 98 fn. 18.
sources.note: Second-hand report on the only earlier accent note for the area: 'The only place where I am aware of any mention is in Nekes & Worms (2006:67), where there is an exceedingly brief discussion of accentuation amounting to less than half a page. It is stated that accent - one infers in the standard average Australian language - falls on the first syllable of a word, and sometimes a secondary accent falls on the fourth syllable. A few illustrative examples are given in Nyulnyul.' Jabirrjabirr is not named in this connection.

sources.citation: Bowern, Claire. 2010. Two missing pieces in a Nyulnyulan jigsaw puzzle. LSA Annual Meeting Extended Abstracts 1: 48:1-5.
sources.note: Nothing. The two 'missing pieces' are Nimanburru and Ngumbarl, not Jabirrjabirr; §3.1 Phonology discusses vowel length and *ŋk > ŋ only. Confirms Nekes & Worms 2006 (reprint of 1953) as the source for the central Dampier Land languages.

sources.citation: Stokes, Bronwyn & William McGregor. 2003. Classification and subclassification of the Nyulnyulan languages. In N. Evans (ed.), The non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia, 29-74. Pacific Linguistics 552.
sources.note: Nothing language-specific. p. 32: 'JABIRRJABIRR Nekes and Worms (1953) is the major source; a few items also appear in Kerr (n.d.)'. One comparative aside (p. 66) that an initial syllable 'would almost certainly have borne stress' in the proto-language.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, inventory ER 2699 'Jabirr-Jabirr' (contributor Erich Round), source record mcgregor_nyulnyul_1996 = McGregor, William. [1996]. Nyulnyul. Languages of the World/Materials 88. Lincom Europa.
sources.note: Segment inventory (20 segments) only; no stress or suprasegmental information. Shows that Round's Jabirr-Jabirr inventory is drawn from McGregor's 1996 LINCOM Nyulnyul sketch (which also serves for Ngumbarl, Nimanburu, Jawi and Nyulnyul).

sources.citation: McGregor, William. 1988. Handbook of Kimberley languages, vol. 1: General information. Pacific Linguistics C-105. §4.5 Jabirrjabirr / Djaber-Djaber, pp. 63-65.
sources.note: Nothing on Jabirrjabirr. Source inventory only: word lists (Capell 1966, Kerr n.d., Nekes 1931-47, 1939, Worms 1938-1959), textual material Nekes & Worms 1953, and 'Grammar or sketch grammar: None'; 'apparently a handful of speakers remain'.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page dyab1238; Wikipedia 'Jabirr Jabirr language'; PHOIBLE language page dyab1238.
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog lists no grammar/phonology/sketch (n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0); Wikipedia has no phonology section and cites only Bowern 2012 (Bardi), Stokes & McGregor 2003, AIATSIS K8.
